title: Closed immersion of the Over-base-changed diagonal detects separatedness
statement: Let S,T be schemes [def-pc-scheme], g:T→S a morphism, X→S and Y→S schemes over S, and f:X→Y an S-morphism. Give X ×_Y X [def-pc-fibre-product] its structure map to S using the second projection to X. Let γ:X→X ×_Y X be the diagonal as an S-morphism. Then the base change γ_T along g [def-pc-base-change] is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] if and only if the base change f_T is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. No compactness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01ZQ, lemma-descend-separated-finite-presentation, proof: diagonal base-change identification; expanded by the agent directly from fibre-product universal properties

proof.text: Form the two base-changed projections a,b from (X ×_Y X) ×_S T to X ×_S T. Their composites with the base-changed f agree, giving e to (X ×_S T) ×_{Y ×_S T} (X ×_S T). Conversely the latter object has two components to X and equal components to T; these give v in the reverse direction. Checking both projections twice proves e and v are inverse. This uses only the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] and base-change definition [def-pc-base-change].

The base-changed diagonal composed with e equals the diagonal of the base-changed f, by checking its two projections. Closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] are invariant under composition with isomorphisms. Separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism] is precisely the closed-immersion property of this diagonal, yielding the equivalence. The Lean proof constructs and checks the isomorphism explicitly.

lean.statement:
theorem isClosedImmersion_overPullback_diagonal_iff
    {S T : Scheme.{u}} (g : T ⟶ S) (X Y : Over S) (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    IsClosedImmersion
        (((Over.pullback g).map
          (Over.homMk (pullback.diagonal f.left) (by simp) :
            X ⟶ Over.mk (pullback.snd f.left f.left ≫ X.hom))).left) ↔
      IsSeparated (((Over.pullback g).map f).left)
